content.comment_body: I created an application on my PC for a [product_name] version 5, 12/24RCo (no display). My customer and the end user are not interested in programming, but I'd like them to have a backup in case the device fails and must be reprogrammed. I purchased some yellow eprom modules but can't figure out how to program them without a display on the [product_name]. The documentation says an empty [product_name]-pure will load the program from the eprom module on startup, but how do I initially write to the module? After programming the module, if I later update the application via PC and cable, how can I overwrite the program on the eprom module in the [product_name]-pure? If the only option is to buy a [product_name] with a display just for this, do I need to get an identical setup (including any expansion modules I used) as the original?
Hello! I believe you'll need a [product_name] with a display or a [product_name] Prommer.

The original application uses a DM16 expansion module. If I get a [product_name] with a display to program a memory module, will the application still download properly even though the expansion module isn't attached?
Hello! The absence of the expansion module shouldn't impact the process.
@[user_name]: For this, you need the new memory card, order number [article_no] (the brown one) for [product_name] versions 0BA4 and 0BA5. The old yellow version isn't compatible with 0BA4/0BA5.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges backing up and restoring applications on [product_name] units without displays, due to incompatibilities between memory modules and unclear programming steps for display-less versions. There’s uncertainty about which memory modules to use and about program transfer procedures, especially when expansion modules are part of the setup. Guidance on programming and updating memory modules for these models needs clarification.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect it to be straightforward to back up and restore applications on [product_name] units without a display, using compatible and easy-to-program memory modules, without additional hardware purchases. They also want clear and simple instructions for handling updates when applications are modified.
